source_title: Zimmer Biomet to Preview the Next Era of Intelligent Orthopedic Surgery at AAHKS 2026
source_excerpt:
Featured symposium will reveal a new vision for intelligent systems that support surgeon judgment, reduce procedural burden and connect the episode of care
WARSAW, Ind. , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc. (NYSE and SIX: ZBH) today announced its plans to host a featured symposium and booth discussions to reveal a new vision for intelligent orthopedic surgery at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons (AAHKS), taking place November 5â8 in the Dallas area.
At its symposium on November 6, Zimmer Biomet will preview an emerging technology category that looks beyond individual robotic capabilities toward a more intelligent, connected approach to orthopedic careâone designed around the surgeon's expertise, judgment and control.
"Over the past decade, surgical planning, navigation and robotics have fundamentally changed how we perform surgery, but precision alone isn't the end goal," said Jonathan Vigdorchik, M.D., Chief Science, Technology and Medical Affairs Officer at Zimmer Biomet. Today, we know which patients do well, but we don't always know exactly how their surgery was performed or which surgical decisions contributed to their outcomes. We need to move beyond a surgeon's subjective assessment of a successful operation to objectively measuring what happened in the operating room and connecting those decisions to how the patient recovered. That's where we see the opportunity for intelligent systems: helping surgeons make better-informed decisions, translating their intent into action and reducing the procedural burden. Ultimately, we want to create a continuous feedback loop between surgical decisions and patient recovery, so that what we learn from every patient helps us deliver better care for the next."
Throughout the day, visitors can explore the thought-provoking new approach at the company's booth (#608), examining Zimmer Biomet's vision for how intelligent surgical systems may help expand capabilities without adding complexity, cognitive load or physical burdens.
Zimmer Biomet's unveiling of a new category in orthopedic surgery aims to address these challenges with a simple principle: transfer burden, not control.

Important Safety Information for Oxford Cementless Partial Knee:
The Oxford Â® Cementless Partial Knee System is indicated for use in unilateral knee procedures with osteoarthritis or avascular necrosis limited to the medial compartment of the knee. It is intended to be implanted without the application of bone cement for patients whose clinical condition would benefit from a shorter surgical time compared to the cemented implant. The Oxford Partial Knee is not indicated for use in the lateral compartment or for patients with ligament deficiency, or for use in simultaneous bilateral surgery or planned staged bilateral procedures. Potential risks include, but are not limited to, loosening, dislocation, fracture, wear and infection, any of which can require additional surgery. For a full list of product indications, contraindications and warnings, please see the associated product Instructions For Use (IFU).
